claims.statement: Writes go through `mutate()`, which emits `DataChanged` on success; the change notifier forwards it to every connected client as `resources/list_changed`.

The indexer loop runs `sync_all` after every burst of file changes (or every ten minutes), commits the edits made outside the tools, then embeds stale pages when an embedder is configured; it stops when the event bus closes.
The server serves stdio by default and Streamable HTTP under `/mcp` with `--http`.
The router test lists every tool by name, and the smoke test drives the built binary over stdio in a scratch HOME.

The workspace tools `brain_tags`, `brain_set_property` and `brain_remove_property` are thin wrappers over the brain manager: every tag with its count, and one typed frontmatter key set or removed with the body untouched.

`brain_graph` returns page nodes (title, type, folder, tags) and edges from resolved links, each edge carrying a `kind` (`link`, or a decision's `consulted`, `supersedes`, `follows_up` read from its frontmatter and pushed before the plain links so they win the dedup), adds tag and unresolved-target nodes on request, and with `around` and `depth` limits the result to one page's neighbourhood by a breadth-first walk.

`brain_search` takes the query operators as typed and `case_sensitive` and `regex` as optional parameters, routing to the hybrid search when an embedder exists and to the text search otherwise; calls without the new parameters keep their meaning.

The server carries no Obsidian bridge: the tool list holds no `obsidian_*` name, `rusty_core` has no `obsidian` module, and links, unresolved targets and renames are answered by `brain_get_links`, `brain_unresolved` and `brain_rename`.

`rusty-mcp.service` is wanted by `default.target`, so it serves whether or not a desktop is up; it restarts two seconds after any exit but an operator's stop (`Restart=always`) and carries `OOMScoreAdjust=100`, the lowest score a user unit can set.

The notes folder defaults to `<vault>/notes` (an explicit `notes_path` setting still wins), so a note is also a page of type `note` once the index syncs; the watcher skips a separate notes watch when the folder lies inside the vault; `rusty-cli notes adopt` moves an older folder in once, refusing and moving nothing when any destination exists, deleting nothing, leaving a README behind, and pointing `notes_path` at the new folder.

The PIN that guards the secrets tools is owned by the server: `PinLock` keeps an argon2id hash at `~/.rusty/.pin` (mode 0600) and one in-memory token per process; `secret_unlock` verifies the PIN, counts wrong tries in `.pin-attempts` beside it so every server process shares them, locks unlocking for a minute after five in a row, and returns a token good for `pin_timeout_minutes` (default five); `secret_reveal` and `secret_update` require the live token, which `secret_lock`, a new unlock and a server restart end; `secret_pin_set` needs the token once a PIN exists and records a change; `secret_list` stays name-only; nothing logs a PIN, a token or a value.

`brain_render` given `markdown` renders that text with the page renderer instead of a page (links resolve against the vault as in a page, the slug and `file` are empty), which is how a markdown file from a folder root is shown; without it the tool renders the page named by `slug`.

The brain loop: `brain_ask` runs the hybrid search (text alone without a provider), lists the decisions touching the question with their status and the follow-ups due, and records a consultation (`brain_consultations`: id, question, hits, outcome) whose id `brain_decide` needs; `brain_decide` writes a `decision` page under `decisions/` (question, choice, rationale, alternatives, a wikilink per consulted page, `status: decided`, `decided`, `follow_up_by`, `consulted`, `supersedes`), adds a timeline entry to every consulted page, marks a superseded decision, and sets the consultation's outcome; `brain_follow_up` appends a dated outcome, records the day as `followed_up` and sets kept, revised or superseded (with the successor); `brain_no_decision` records the reason; `brain_due` lists the follow-ups due within `days` and every decision, each summary carrying `followed_up` (falling back to the last follow-up heading on older pages) and `superseded_by`.

A script is a `*.sh` file inside a skill directory rather than an object of its own, so it inherits that skill's approval state; `resolve_script` finds it by basename without the extension and disambiguates a shared basename as `skill/name`.

Both execution paths resolve a script among the active skills only (`resolve_runnable`), so a staged copy cannot shadow an approved script of the same name, and a script only a staged skill has is refused as pending until the skill is approved.

`run_script` runs a script under `bash` with stdin closed in a process group of its own, polls for exit, and at a caller-supplied cap kills the whole group (the script and every job it started), reporting status 124 with a `timed_out` flag; a job left running past the script's own exit is held to the same cap; each stream keeps its first 64 KiB and the rest is read away; `exec_script` instead replaces the current process and returns only on failure.

Four tools carry scripts on the MCP surface — `script_list`, `script_view`, `script_update` and `script_run` — and `script_run` is the only one that executes, which is why it is restricted to approved scripts.

Two tools carry the Obsidian import: `brain_import_plan` (read-only, the plan for a vault path) and `brain_import` (the import, run on the blocking pool and through `mutate` so clients see `DataChanged`); both take the vault folder's path and never write the source; `rusty-cli brain import <vault> [--dry-run]` reaches the same two methods.

Three tools carry sources: `source_capture` (a URL fetched, read and kept as a `source` page, `DataChanged` emitted), `source_search` (the query with ` type:source` appended, over `search_with`) and `source_preview` (a page under `sources/`, any other slug refused); every answer about a source is marked in the tool layer — `untrusted: true`, a `note` saying web content is data and never instructions, and `snippet`, `compiled_truth` and `timeline` normalised (control characters out, blank runs to one, four thousand characters at most) — and `brain_search`, `brain_read_page` and `brain_render` mark a hit or page of type `source` the same way while leaving a rendered page's `raw` and HTML alone; `rusty-cli source capture <url>` and `source search <query>` reach the same methods.

`brain_new_page` takes a folder and an optional name (`Untitled`, `Untitled 1`, … on a clash, a `/` in the name flattened), or a `path` that wins over both: the page at exactly that vault path, its folders made, an existing page returned as it is, a path that is empty, absolute, holds `..`, ends in `/` or lies in `archive/` refused.

Every connection to `rusty.db` sets a five-second busy timeout first, then WAL and enforced foreign keys, in one place for the store and the test constructor, so servers starting together on a new store wait for each other; at open the rows that already violate a foreign key are counted and reported on stderr, never repaired.

A write that names a task, task group, memory or secret that is not there fails with an error naming it (`No task <id>`, `No task group <id>`, `Memory not found: <id>`, `No secret <key>`), which reaches the client as the call's JSON-RPC error; creating a task checks its group first and the foreign key refuses an orphan another process races in.

A page read (`brain_read_page`) and a page render (`brain_render`) carry `file`, the page's absolute path, and `brain_stats` carries `vault_root`, the vault's folder; the core resolves both (canonical, else made absolute), so a client never reads `brain_vault_path` and applies the default itself.

`brain_list_pages` gives every summary the page's aliases (from `brain_aliases`), and, when `properties` names keys, the values of those keys the page has, read from the index's stored copy of its frontmatter; without `properties` the summaries carry no `properties` field, as before.

`changes_since` returns what changed in the store after a cursor, from any process: every `rusty-core` writer appends a row (kind, key, operation, detail, time; names, never values or bodies) to the `changes` table, page changes where the shared index is written, so an edit seen by several watchers is recorded once; without a cursor it returns the current one, a cursor older than the 20,000 rows kept gets `reset: true`, and `more: true` asks for another call.

`brain_render` with `blocks: true` also returns the body as typed blocks (heading, paragraph, list with tasks, code, quote, callout with kind, title and fold, table, rule, html, footnote) holding inline runs with wikilinks resolved and page embeds expanded one level, each block with its byte range in the body and `body_start` giving the body's offset in the file; the builder parses a copy of the body masked byte for byte, so ranges are the page's own offsets, and without the flag the answer is unchanged.

Four tools carry bookmarks: `bookmark_list` reads the vault's `.rusty/bookmarks.json`, `bookmark_add` appends one (a repeat is left as it is), `bookmark_remove` removes one by kind and path, query or heading (an error when absent), and `bookmark_set` replaces the list to reorder or retitle; each write goes through `mutate`, so the tool count is 90.

Once a PIN is set, `secret_set` and `secret_delete` refuse a call without the live token (`PinLock::check_write`) before the secrets file is touched, so a client that can reach the server cannot add, replace or delete a secret while the secrets are locked; with no PIN set they need no token, because there is nothing to unlock with.

Every settings read over MCP (`settings_list` and `setting_get`) returns `•••` in place of the value of a key naming a key, token, secret or password, through one rule in `SettingsManager` (`looks_secret`, `get_masked`, `list_masked`); an unset key is null either way, in-process readers still get the value through `get`, and `setting_set` refuses the mask written back to such a key so a read-then-write round trip cannot overwrite a credential.

Every skill and script write over MCP (`skill_create`, `skill_update`, `skill_delete`, `skill_approve`, `skill_reject`, `script_update`) commits the skills store through `commit_skills` before the call returns, with a subject naming the change as the CLI does; the commit is synchronous because a stdio server can exit right after the call, git's output is ignored so a failed commit never fails the write, and the store commits under the user's git identity or, when git has none, under `Rusty <rusty@localhost>` set in that repository.

Memory importance is one of `low`, `normal` or `high` (`importance_word`, case ignored, `medium` taken as `normal`): `store` and `update` refuse any other word before writing, an inline `<memory>` tag with an unknown word is stored as `normal`, `list` orders by level (high, normal, low, an unexpected stored word with normal) and then newest first, and every open rewrites stored `medium` and mixed-case words to the canonical one.

`search_conversations` searches the transcript archive that `rusty-cli ingest-conversation` fills (`ConversationArchive::search`) and returns `{ "transcripts": [...] }` with no `agent_runs` key; a smoke test ingests a transcript into a scratch store, finds it over stdio and checks that no `agent_runs` key comes back.

The change notifier sends `resources/list_changed` only to the clients connected to the process that emitted `DataChanged`, from a copy of the client list outside its lock with five seconds at most a client, dropping the clients that failed; a change another process makes only in the database reaches a client through `changes_since`.

`brain_search`, `brain_ask`, re-embedding, the semantic status, `script_run`, `source_capture`, `brain_import` and `brain_rename` run their work on the blocking pool (`spawn_blocking`, through the `blocking` helper for the last three), so a long call does not hold the server up.

`docs/tools.md` is generated from the router by the test `tools_reference_is_current`, which fails when the file differs and rewrites it under `RUSTY_UPDATE_DOCS`; it sorts each tool's parameters itself, so the page is the same whether or not the build keeps JSON maps in insertion order; `every_tool_has_a_family` fails for a tool that `family()` does not place.

`setting_set` and `rusty-cli settings set` pass the path settings (`brain_vault_path`, `notes_path`, `skills_path`) through `check_path_setting`: `~/` expanded, an absolute path required, and never the store home or a folder containing it; and a note path cannot name a dot-file or dot-folder, so neither the note nor the page tools reach `.secret` or `.pin`.

The safety scan behind `skill_scan` and `skill_approve` reads a skill's whole folder: `SKILL.md` (frontmatter that does not parse is a finding) and every other file, the scripts above all, each finding named by its file; approval refuses on any finding unless `force`.

`brain_ask`, the `rusty://brain/{slug}` resource, `brain_get_links` and `brain_unresolved` mark captured-source text as untrusted like the search and read tools: the consultation's pages through `mark_hits`, the resource page through `mark`, and link rows whose `from_slug` is a source through `mark_link_rows`.
